source.text: General Atomic report GA-7882, Kinetic Behavior of TRIGA Reactors (1967), Table VII, page 31, modified Fuchs-Nordheim model (C = C0 + C1 T), $3 pulse (delta k prompt 0.014): peak power 2130 MW, burst energy 26.1 MW s, temperature rise of the burst 262 C (parameters: lifetime 4e-5 s, C0 = 8e4 W s/C at 25 C, C1 = 1.5e2 W s/C^2, alpha = 1e-4 per C per core). The hottest fuel is the start temperature of 25 C plus the published rise (the interior of a pulse of some 15 ms is adiabatic: the diffusion time over the radius is seconds).
source.check: Cross-check: tests/gaKineticsTable.test.ts derives the same model exactly (Simpson's rule) and gets 2131.5 MW, 26.19 MW s and a rise of 262.7 C; FEED's generator agrees with that to 1e-4. The report's numbers are rounded and its equation 16 for the rise is an approximation, so the tolerance is 0.5 %.

coverage.domain: TRIGA-like core of the report GA-7882 (Table VII): $3 pulse, prompt neutrons only (no delayed groups), constant prompt coefficient of -1e-4 per K, heat capacity C = C0 + C1 T, 60 ms window (the pulse is over in about 45 ms), initial power 100 kW (about 5e-5 of the peak: the report neglects it); the core is 720 pins of 1 m, the pin an illustrative synthetic one
